title: The Password
text: I really should have looked into which room in Faubrey belonged to the Crimson Swine beforehand. But it never occurred to me that I’d need such utterly useless knowledge for a future like this! No helping it now—I’d just have to infiltrate the dorm management office and dig up whatever records seemed relevant. Apparently it was right before the long holiday break, so the students didn’t seem to be attending many classes anyway. The dorm head was a pig, but since she was older than the students, she was easy enough to distinguish from the faculty within the dorm.
And on that pig dorm head’s desk… there were outing records! What a stroke of luck, I say. Time to search for the Crimson Swine’s name. The Crimson Swine’s name… was Witch, I believe.

Hm? There was a student named Sconbu Witch. Judging by the position, that had to be a surname. What a peculiar family name. Vinegared-Kelp Witch, indeed. “What exactly are you looking at?” Father in my head scolded me, even as he admitted—hmm, that really is an amusing family name—with obvious interest. “How pointless…” he muttered, though I had a feeling Ren and Itsuki were also stifling laughter at the name. Should I keep collecting Japanese-standard gag surnames to share with Father once we’re reunited?
“Nano, Rival just remembered what you were originally looking for.”
Gah—Rival, how is it that you show up even inside my own memories!? You’re noisy even inside my own head, I say!
“Dunno nano. Rival thinks you’d better hurry up and search, nano.”
Silence, I say! A Brionac straight to memory-Rival’s face!
“Even this time, if you send the egg to another world, remember it, nano—!”

I’ll do it again this time too! You just keep that world of yours peaceful, nano. I absolutely will not let you come to this world again, not this time. Hmm… nothing about the name “Witch” makes me think it’s actually her, does it?
“Wrong name, nano.”

So I said silence, mental Rival. Nobody summoned you. Persistent creature. But still… her surname should be the same as the Queen’s and my Fiancée’s. Let’s see, if I recall correctly, it was the same as the country name itself—Melromarc. So I scrolled through the surname search.

And then… there it was. Malty Melromarc… was that the name? Let’s see… room number—no, wait, according to this record, her current status is… she’s already completed the paperwork to return to her homeland! Damn that Crimson Swine! Isn’t she leaving awfully early?

That’s what I thought, but Melromarc was quite far from here. On Filolial-sama’s legs it’d take over two weeks, though using transportation would speed things up. More importantly, knowing the Crimson Swine, she’d probably take all sorts of detours along the way back. Ugh… an early assassination was shaping up to be more trouble than expected. Still, knowing her, she was surely causing mischief all along the route too, wasn’t she?

Here’s what I’ll do, I say. I’ll rely on those shady types around Faubrey and Zeltoble—the ones who’ll sell information for coin, no questions asked, no strings attached. Why do I know about people like that, you ask? Of course, it’s from the accumulated loops, back when Father was mingling with monster merchants. In the previous loop, Itsuki had connections with them too, so the memory’s still fresh. They were active in Shieldfreeden but kept showing their faces around Faubrey as well.

Based on that memory, I’d go to an information broker and have them track down the Crimson Swine’s whereabouts. For that, I needed… to go to a monster nest and earn some cash! Right now I’m completely broke, after all. I don’t even have enough money to purchase Filolial-sama’s kin, so it’s time to earn, I say! Once I left the academy, I dropped my concealment and raised my spear high.
“Here we go!”

And so I charged into a monster nest to earn some money, I say. While I was at it, I’d hunt some griffins too! Not that leveling up was the goal—in that sense, the experience points would go to waste. I wanted to secure Yuki-chan and the other Filolial-sama as quickly as possible. With that in mind, I headed off—just as before—to the region deep in the mountains where dangerous monsters dwelt.
Unlike the dragon-hunting grounds I’d visited before, this region was home to mostly griffins and dinosaur-type monsters.
“Meteor Thrust X! Brionac X! Gungnir X! Hahahaha! Weak, far too weak!”
“You dare rampage in my territory! For the crime of trespassing, you shall pay with your—”
“Brionac X!”
“Guwah—!?”
“I’ll send your daughter along after you soon enough, I say!”
Fuhahahaha! Another big griffin down! Of course, I slaughtered everyone in the surrounding area too! Having said that, I proceeded to loot the nest for anything valuable.
“Y-you! I will never forgive you!”
As I was ransacking the nest… something that looked vaguely familiar took griffin form and lunged at me. Probably one of Takt’s griffin companions.
“Oh, how convenient that you happened to be here! Drop dead, I say! Brionac X!”
“Wha—that weapon, don’t tell me it’s one of the Legendary—”
Squelch! Takt’s griffin went down! What luck that she happened to be back visiting home—her misfortune, truly!
“I’ll send Takt along after you soon too, fuhahaha.”

Well, more precisely, it’d be better to let the Pig King handle the disposal. I had a nagging feeling I was forgetting something, though. Disposing of them early would minimize the damage, wouldn’t it? The question was whether the claws were in her hands. If my memory served correctly, Wolf became a combat slave quite a while back—earlier than this point in time, I believe. Anyway, between the griffins and the dragon’s treasure hoard, my funds were secured. The problem was I’d gathered so much I couldn’t carry it all, making it a hassle to hide. Well… I’d just come back for the rest when needed.
“Money secured, I say!”

With that settled, I wasted no time making contact with an information broker in Zeltoble, which was easier to approach as an entry point. I covered my entire body in a robe to make sure my identity was completely unidentifiable. I figured going through the monster merchant’s introduction would work too, but I didn’t want to waste time going through intermediaries, so I’d move swiftly. Still… precisely because this was the underworld, I wanted to avoid having my trail picked up in turn. The easy route would be extracting the information and then silencing them, but even in the world’s underworld, that sort of method shouldn’t be done. Well, the Crimson Swine had plenty of enemies, so surely it’d be hard to pin anything on me specifically? Still, I figured I should do my best to keep my speech as nondescript as possible. And so, regarding the information broker matter, I headed to the assassins’ guild.
“…What do you want? This is a members-only tavern. Membership card?”
I’d hidden my spear, draped myself in a full-body robe, and even taken the extra care of donning a mask before arriving at the entrance to the assassins’ guild.
“I’m looking for someone. I heard this is the place to ask.”
I wanted to say “I say,” but I held back.
“…I don’t know where you heard that, but I can’t help you based on rumors like that. No such thing exists here.”
Playing dumb, were we? If it were someone with underworld connections, they’d have arranged things easily enough.
“Don’t say that… wasn’t it, ‘That clan has so many identical faces, it’s downright terrifying—like the women at every healing facility across the land’?”

And so, while pressing coin into their palm, I whispered the secret password I knew from accumulated loop knowledge. Apparently it was some kind of specialized code language. For the record, I had no idea what it actually meant, but Father, upon seeing the monster merchant’s face back then, had seemed to understand something about it.
“What’s the deal with that password? I get the sentiment, but… who on earth came up with it?”
“It’s one of this guild’s passwords. Yes. Apparently it’s a phrase the dark guild members sometimes agree upon. Yes.”
That’s what I’d been told. Who on earth came up with this password, I wonder?
“That’s—… come in.”

Ah, success, I say. And so, once inside the building, I was led to a room with a stark, unadorned counter. …Several people were hiding about. Using a flushing-out spell to take them down would’ve been simple enough, but that wasn’t my objective here.
